title: Frequent changing of Window Icon slows Plasmashell if TaskManager is present on a panel
line: A window that changes its icon many times per second no longer makes Plasma slow, eat memory and finally crash.
explanation: On Wayland every icon_changed event from KWin made the task model open a new pipe, ask KWin for the icon and queue a thread-pool read; with an icon changing every 10 ms these piled up until plasmashell hit its open-file limit and the Wayland connection died. Each change also evicted the window's cached app data, so the .desktop file lookup was redone on every update, and every new icon went to QML (about 200 per second), where the old QIcon copies are only freed by the JS garbage collector, so memory climbed by about 5 MB/s. Now a window reads at most one icon at a time and waits 100 ms before reading the next one (the latest icon is always fetched in the end), and the window's own icon is no longer stored in the app data cache, so icon changes don't drop it.

commits.message:
libtaskmanager: limit how often Wayland window icons are re-read

A window that changes its icon very often made plasmashell open a pipe
for each change, until it ran out of file descriptors and died. Now one
icon is read at a time, at most every 100 ms, without dropping app data.

BUG: 487390

media.caption: Master: a window changing its icon every 10 ms (top right) drives plasmashell to 110-200% CPU, memory grows ~5 MB/s and open files start climbing
With the fix, same window: plasmashell stays at ~9% CPU, memory stays flat, open files steady; the task icon still follows the window's icon
Master, a few seconds later: plasmashell died ('Too many open files'), the panel is gone and the launcher can't open
With the fix, after a minute of icon changes: the panel is fine and the launcher opens normally
Master: full run with the live plasmashell monitor, ending with plasmashell crashing
With the fix: full run with the live monitor, plasmashell stays light and responsive

review.text: Excellent root-cause fix in WaylandTasksModel that serializes and rate-limits Wayland icon pipe reads to one in-flight request per window with a 100 ms cooldown while preserving the trailing update, and removes the unnecessary appDataCache icon write and eviction on every iconChanged event. QObject context lifetimes for both the QFutureWatcher connection and QTimer::singleShot are safe against window destruction, and pipe2 failure does not wedge iconRequested. Before/after monitors and autotests convincingly confirm the elimination of the CPU spike, memory climb, and FD-exhaustion crash.

reviews.text: Excellent root-cause fix in WaylandTasksModel that serializes and rate-limits Wayland icon pipe reads to one in-flight request per window with a 100 ms cooldown while preserving the trailing update, and removes the unnecessary appDataCache icon write and eviction on every iconChanged event. QObject context lifetimes for both the QFutureWatcher connection and QTimer::singleShot are safe against window destruction, and pipe2 failure does not wedge iconRequested. Before/after monitors and autotests convincingly confirm the elimination of the CPU spike, memory climb, and FD-exhaustion crash.

Targets the actual Wayland cause left after the X11-only 6.1.2 fix: every icon_changed opened a pipe and queued a read with no bound, and each change also evicted the window's app data cache. Now there is at most one read in flight per window, a 100 ms trailing throttle that always fetches the latest icon, and the window's own icon is no longer stored in (and evicted from) appDataCache, which is safe because AppData.icon is only read in icon(). The QTimer is bound to the PlasmaWindow, so it is gone with the window. Before/after monitor captures show the CPU/RSS/fd growth and 'Too many open files' crash gone while the task icon still follows the window; since it is in the shared model the pager benefits too. Client-side rate limiting in libtaskmanager is the right place given KWin declined to throttle.
